lean.statement:
∀ (d N : ℕ),
  1 ≤ N →
    2 * N + 1 ≤ d + 1 →
      ∀ (β : ℝ),
        0 < β →
          ∀ (x₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d + 1))),
            have f := fun y =>
              have v := y - x₀;
              β / 4 *
                ((v.ofLp 0 ^ 2 + ∑ i, (v.ofLp i.castSucc - v.ofLp i.succ) ^ 2 + v.ofLp (Fin.last d) ^ 2) / 2 -
                  v.ofLp 0);
            have xstar := x₀ + WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => 1 - (↑↑i + 1) / (↑d + 2);
            ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
              ContDiff ℝ 1 f ∧
                IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
                  (∀ (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d + 1))),
                      f y ≤ f x + inner ℝ (gradient f x) (y - x) + β / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
                    ∀ (x : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d + 1))),
                      x 0 = x₀ →
                        (∀ (n : ℕ), x (n + 1) - x₀ ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => gradient f (x ↑i))) →
                          1 / 8 * ‖x 0 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖x N - xstar‖ ^ 2
approved_definition_context: EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) is real m-dimensional Euclidean space with the usual real inner product and norm. Fin indices start at zero. castSucc and succ map an index to the same index or its successor in the next larger finite type.
WithLp.toLp 2 equips a coordinate vector with the Euclidean norm without changing entries. ofLp recovers the coordinate vector. Fin.last d is the index d in Fin (d+1).

ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ means global convexity; ContDiff ℝ 1 means continuously Fréchet differentiable; IsMinOn f Set.univ means global minimization. gradient is the Riesz gradient for a differentiable real-valued function on this Euclidean space.
Submodule.span ℝ of a set is its real linear span; Set.range over Fin (n+1) ranges over indices zero through n. The pretty-printed local have expressions are definitional bindings, not hypotheses.
